speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and fatigue; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present and how would you rate their severity on a scale of one to ten?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the worsening fatigue toward the end of the day is concerning. You mentioned recent travel, hiking, camping, and multiple illnesses—have you noticed any specific triggers like high altitudes, insect bites, or unexplained weight loss alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The combination of weakness and fatigue that worsens throughout the day, specifically accompanied by mild diplopia (double vision), is highly characteristic of Myasthenia Gravis. To confirm this, I need to see the results of an Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test and a Chest CT scan to rule out thymoma.
